limitations.title: Shared buffers are not hardware coherent
limitations.impact: Stale reads or loss of dirty data across CPU/DMA ownership changes.
limitations.trigger: Concurrent cached CPU access and non-snooping DMA/LP access.
limitations.workaround: Use exclusive ownership, whole cache-block ranges, directional cache maintenance and fences.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed v0.4 PRODUCT snapshot; MPW differences are stated separately.

limitations.title: HP loader has no firmware-local ready timeout
limitations.impact: LP can wait indefinitely for the expected Linux mailbox event.
limitations.trigger: No mailbox message after HP release.
limitations.workaround: Use the simulator deadline during acceptance. A board supervisor/watchdog policy is integration work; no automatic retry is implemented here.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed v0.4 PRODUCT snapshot; MPW differences are stated separately.

limitations.title: Boot CRC is not authentication
limitations.impact: A CRC-valid image is not proven to come from a trusted signer.
limitations.trigger: Untrusted image or writable external boot storage.
limitations.workaround: Treat signing, key storage, rollback prevention and secure recovery as separate unimplemented system requirements.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed v0.4 PRODUCT snapshot; MPW differences are stated separately.

limitations.title: Native Linux peripheral coverage is incomplete
limitations.impact: A HAL or DT node does not provide a native Linux driver.
limitations.trigger: Applications attempt direct Linux use of a custom peripheral.
limitations.workaround: Use the published support matrix, retain LP ownership where needed, and validate a platform driver before handoff.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed v0.4 PRODUCT snapshot; MPW differences are stated separately.

limitations.title: Resource reset request is not universal engine reset
limitations.impact: Some downstream peripheral engines are not reset by the central lifecycle request.
limitations.trigger: Using Resource CONTROL.RESET as independent engine reset containment.
limitations.workaround: Drain and use each IP reset/recovery contract. APU P1 has a local reset connection; do not generalize it to all engines.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed v0.4 PRODUCT snapshot; MPW differences are stated separately.

limitations.title: Forced HP reset can discard dirty cache state
limitations.impact: Missing cache-clean acknowledgement prevents preservation of modified shared data.
limitations.trigger: HP shutdown times out before acknowledgement.
limitations.workaround: Keep a recoverable authoritative copy outside dirty HP cache; treat timed-out work as failed and reinitialize dependent queues.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed v0.4 PRODUCT snapshot; MPW differences are stated separately.

limitations.title: QPI and OPI cannot operate together
limitations.impact: The inactive memory window returns an error and its pads are disconnected.
limitations.trigger: Accessing the inactive memory mode or attempting a live protocol change.
limitations.workaround: Select the mode at boot before use; respect the sticky lock. A live handover is not supported.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed v0.4 PRODUCT snapshot; MPW differences are stated separately.

limitations.title: Generic FPGA routes do not qualify every interface
limitations.impact: Dedicated USB2 ULPI and SDIO1 pads need board assignment and electrical/timing review.
limitations.trigger: Assuming logical pads are FPGA ball or package-pin assignments.
limitations.workaround: Supply board constraints, bank voltages, external devices and validated timing before enabling a physical route.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed v0.4 PRODUCT snapshot; MPW differences are stated separately.

limitations.title: APU production codec jobs remain disabled
limitations.impact: The register shell and bounded codec/transport work do not establish a complete media product.
limitations.trigger: Submitting unsupported production codec or KWS jobs.
limitations.workaround: Check the implemented capability and job result; use only the bounded supported path described in the APU chapter.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed v0.4 PRODUCT snapshot; MPW differences are stated separately.

limitations.title: Integrated RNG entropy is unqualified
limitations.impact: Deterministic test data cannot supply production cryptographic entropy.
limitations.trigger: Using the current entropy stream to generate secret keys or nonces.
limitations.workaround: Keep diagnostic use separate; production entropy requires a reviewed physical source and qualification.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed v0.4 PRODUCT snapshot; MPW differences are stated separately.

limitations.title: Physical operating limits are not characterized
limitations.impact: Configuration clocks and behavioral models are not electrical or silicon ratings.
limitations.trigger: Selecting board voltage, frequency, thermal or timing limits from RTL defaults.
limitations.workaround: Use approved technology, macro, package and board reports; leave absent specifications TBD.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed v0.4 PRODUCT snapshot; MPW differences are stated separately.

limitations.title: Legacy PRODUCT window is not an MPW selector
limitations.impact: Legacy selection writes are rejected in PRODUCT.
limitations.trigger: Calling selectable user-core/IP mutators on a fixed PRODUCT configuration.
limitations.workaround: Detect mode/capabilities first and use fixed EXT-L/EXT-H APIs in PRODUCT.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed v0.4 PRODUCT snapshot; MPW differences are stated separately.

limitations.title: Native JPEG master has no normal admission credits
limitations.impact: The dedicated JPEG AXI path is wired to data-master slot 6, but the current crossbar read/write credit functions return zero for that slot. Normal payload addresses cannot be admitted through that route.
limitations.trigger: JPEG private-master traffic routed through the reviewed PRODUCT data plane.
limitations.workaround: Treat end-to-end JPEG private-DMA operation as unavailable on this snapshot. Standalone codec behavior does not prove SoC integration. A separately reviewed RTL change and regression are required; this publication does not change hardware.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed PRODUCT source snapshot; static implementation finding, not silicon measurement.

limitations.title: Rejected EXT-L base writes can change readable state
limitations.impact: READ_BASE and WRITE_BASE next-state assignments are not gated by the KindExtH write-legal result; an EXT-L write can change those readbacks while returning PSLVERR.
limitations.trigger: Writing READ_BASE or WRITE_BASE through the EXT-L register window.
limitations.workaround: Treat these writes as invalid and avoid them. Preserve the slot fault/address when diagnosing an error; do not assume a rejected write rolls back state. EXT-L has no connected data master, so these local outputs do not grant an EXT-L DMA path.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed v0.4 PRODUCT source snapshot; static RTL observation, no new simulation or hardware test.

limitations.title: Generic LP startup has no PSRAM-ready deadline
limitations.impact: Execution can remain before main and before the application writes TEST_STATUS.
limitations.trigger: The generic CRT requests PSRAM initialization and PSRAM_STATUS.READY never becomes set.
limitations.workaround: Confirm the selected startup/linker path, memory-pad selection and external memory readiness; use an external observer deadline. A returned application code cannot describe a stage that was never reached.
limitations.applies_to: Reviewed generic LP CRT; dedicated debug and XPI-loader startups have separate initialization contracts.

reset.label: LP / peripheral clock selection
reset.initial: LP mode resets to 0 (REF24). PCLK divider state is zero, selecting /1 after its reset/configuration path settles.
reset.prerequisites: External reset and reference clocks must satisfy board conditions; local reset must be released.
reset.action: Read clock status/capability before deriving peripheral timing.
reset.observation: Configured rate and observed ready/fault status; not a maximum operating limit.

reset.label: Memory pad mode
reset.initial: MEM_PAD_MODE reset encoding is 1 (QPI); the mode lock resets clear.
reset.prerequisites: The selected external device and its interface clock/reset must be ready.
reset.action: Select the required boot-time mode before memory use; check the lock.
reset.observation: Inactive aperture errors are expected; mode is not a fitted-device probe.

reset.label: HP lifecycle
reset.initial: Controller state Held; HP release, flush and forced-fault state clear.
reset.prerequisites: Root clocks and management MMIO are available.
reset.action: Prepare memory/image and use the controlled release sequence.
reset.observation: Check requested and actual release/reset status; values can change once a request is accepted.

reset.label: Resource owners and locks
reset.initial: OWNER flops reset to 0 (LP); owner lock, quiesce and resource-reset request clear.
reset.prerequisites: PCLK/local reset and the producer/engine status path must be available.
reset.action: Inspect owner, busy/idle and pending status before handoff.
reset.observation: Root ownership is not an independent power/reset guarantee for every engine.

reset.label: Interrupt observation
reset.initial: IRQ outputs depend on peripheral causes, current owner and resource-reset request. A clear initial enable/status can change after an event.
reset.prerequisites: Know each peripheral reset/enable contract and the selected owner route.
reset.action: Install handlers, clear documented stale events, then enable the intended route.
reset.observation: CONTROL.RESET masks owner routes; do not confuse it with an independent controller-wide IRQ enable.

reset.label: Central DMA register context
reset.initial: Channel configuration, byte count, descriptor head/count and IRQ/event enables reset to zero.
reset.prerequisites: PCLK/register path and selected memory/endpoint are available.
reset.action: Probe capability; configure a legal idle context before START.
reset.observation: Zero reset configuration is not a ready-to-start transfer; the core validates width, count, alignment and endpoint.

reset.label: GPIO digital control state
reset.initial: Output data/enable, alternate-function selection and interrupt-enable state use zero-reset Common flops.
reset.prerequisites: Read the selected PDK pad capability and actual board connection.
reset.action: Establish inactive output state, configure ownership/function, then enable the output or interrupt.
reset.observation: An input pad is not guaranteed low; digital reset values do not specify voltage, pull strength or package pins.

reset.label: External-memory initialization
reset.initial: Resetting a controller does not establish a populated, initialized and electrically valid external device.
reset.prerequisites: Correct device/protocol, clocks, pins and timing settings.
reset.action: Follow the controller initialization/probe sequence and wait with its defined timeout.
reset.observation: Use READY/INIT/error and ID where applicable; an address aperture alone proves no device presence.

reset.label: Memory contents and software startup
reset.initial: No universal SRAM/DRAM retention or reset-to-zero content guarantee is published.
reset.prerequisites: The selected memory implementation and loader/linker contract.
reset.action: Initialize software data/BSS and owned buffers before use.
reset.observation: Do not interpret a successful register reset as a memory scrub.

reset.label: Counters and time sources
reset.initial: Counters and status can advance as soon as the relevant clock/reset/enable conditions permit.
reset.prerequisites: Known timebase and the IP-specific coherent read/snapshot sequence.
reset.action: Read a bounded snapshot and establish the software epoch.
reset.observation: A later software read need not equal the reset assignment.

interfaces.excluded: No UHS, DDR, 1.8 V switching, 8-bit bus, MMC/eMMC, tuning/DLL or CQE; hot-remove and combo-card policy are unsupported.
interfaces.software: Initialization, capabilities and speed selection remain software sequenced.
interfaces.evidence: Source-level subset; no compliance report attached

interfaces.title: USB2
interfaces.modes: External ULPI interface; control/bulk/interrupt and single-transaction isochronous paths under the documented role policy.
interfaces.excluded: No integrated analog PHY; high-bandwidth isochronous and HNP/SRP are outside the current scope.
interfaces.software: DCD/HCD primitives and descriptor handling do not imply a complete class stack or USB compliance certificate.
interfaces.evidence: Source-level subset; no compliance report attached

bindings.text: "Dual-role digital controller with external 8-bit ULPI PHY."

interfaces.title: XPI
interfaces.modes: Single/dual/quad data phases, LUT, indirect command/polling and mapped read path.
interfaces.excluded: No DDR/DQS extension or arbitrary memory-mapped NOR writes.
interfaces.software: Use reviewed slot/LUT/device settings; erase/program use the indirect path.
interfaces.evidence: Source-level subset; no compliance report attached

bindings.text: "Four chip-select slots and 16 programmable LUT sequences."

interfaces.title: QPI PSRAM
interfaces.modes: ESP-PSRAM64H SPI/QPI initialization and mapped data operation.
interfaces.excluded: Not a generic controller for every QSPI RAM; shared-pad exclusion applies.
interfaces.software: Probe and initialize each enabled device with the documented recovery sequence.
interfaces.evidence: Source-level subset; no compliance report attached

bindings.text: "Four ESP-PSRAM64H devices addressable through a 32 MiB window."

interfaces.title: OPI / HyperBus-style
interfaces.modes: Octal DDR profile or the modified single-clock HyperBus-style profile.
interfaces.excluded: No live protocol switch or generic commercial HyperBus compatibility claim.
interfaces.software: Protocol encoding, latency and a specific physical device require separate review.
interfaces.evidence: Source-level subset; no compliance report attached

bindings.text: "One octal DDR memory interface and one selected protocol profile."

interfaces.title: SDRAM
interfaces.modes: Fixed geometry, bank tracking, native bursts, initialization/refresh and programmable cycle timings.
interfaces.excluded: DDR/LPDDR and arbitrary geometries are not supported by this interface.
interfaces.software: Match the controller geometry and timing to the selected external component.
interfaces.evidence: Source-level subset; no compliance report attached

bindings.text: "Fixed 64 MiB, x16 SDR geometry with bank/row tracking."

interfaces.title: DVP
interfaces.modes: RGB565/YUV422 byte input, explicit sync, crop/snapshot and word-packed stream output.
interfaces.excluded: No MIPI CSI receiver or automatic colorspace conversion; odd-pixel line DMA is unsupported.
interfaces.software: Sensor byte order and sync configuration must match the capture and consumer layout.
interfaces.evidence: Source-level subset; no compliance report attached

interfaces.title: JPEG
interfaces.modes: 8-bit SOF0 encode/decode and the indexed raster formats; modes are mutually exclusive.
interfaces.excluded: No progressive/lossless/arithmetic/10-12-bit modes. Native SoC DMA admission is currently blocked at slot 6.
interfaces.software: Standalone codec/register behavior is distinct from end-to-end SoC payload availability.
interfaces.evidence: Source-level subset; no compliance report attached

interfaces.title: APU
interfaces.modes: Register/transport and bounded development codec paths described in the IP chapter.
interfaces.excluded: Production codec/KWS jobs remain disabled in the reviewed snapshot.
interfaces.software: A HAL, microcode format or test source does not establish an enabled production audio service.
interfaces.evidence: Source-level subset; no compliance report attached

formats.title: DVP RGB565/YUV422 stream
formats.layout: Two 16-bit pixels occupy a 32-bit word; sensor byte order and FORMAT swap controls determine the pixel value.
formats.boundary: TUSER marks frame start; TLAST marks line end. Odd width yields a partial last word, not a full-word DMA beat.

formats.title: I2S 16-bit stereo words
formats.layout: Older sample in bits 15:0; newer sample in bits 31:16.
formats.boundary: One word carries two samples; channel/sample ordering must match the selected playback/capture convention.

formats.title: I2S 24-bit sample words
formats.layout: One sample in bits 23:0 of a 32-bit container.
formats.boundary: Packed three-byte files require conversion into word containers; no implicit rate conversion.

formats.title: JPEG raster GRAY8
formats.boundary: Stride and job geometry are explicit; no automatic expansion to a different raster format.

formats.title: JPEG raster RGB565
formats.boundary: Check camera byte order before consuming the same named format.

formats.title: JPEG raster RGB888
formats.layout: Bytes R, G, B in order.
formats.boundary: A 32-bit padded RGB layout is not identical to packed RGB888.

bindings.text:
RGB888 byte order is R,
  G, B.

formats.title: JPEG raster YUYV422
formats.boundary: A generic YUV422 label does not select UYVY/YVYU or another byte order.

bindings.text: YUYV is Y0, Cb, Y1, Cr.

formats.title: JPEG raster NV12
formats.layout: Two planes; plane 1 contains interleaved Cb/Cr pairs.
formats.boundary: Use the prescribed byte strides and plane addresses; I420/YV12 are not equivalent.

codes.title: SYSCTRL first-fault reason

meanings.default: Decode/unclassified reason used by the default detail mapping.

codes.observation: FAULT_STATUS.REASON [4:2], only meaningful with PENDING. Capture address, master, write direction and FAULT_DETAIL together.
codes.handling: Preserve the first event before W1C of PENDING. Clearing permits a later event to replace the captured fields; the counter is separate.

codes.title: RIB response / SYSCTRL detail

meanings.RIB_RESP_OK: Successful response; not a fault cause.
meanings.RIB_RESP_BURSTERR: Burst shape/length rejected; SYSCTRL reason uses its default mapping when this detail is captured.

codes.observation: RIB response code; SYSCTRL FAULT_DETAIL preserves the selected fault detail. Its numeric namespace differs from FAULT_STATUS.REASON.
codes.handling: Follow the SYSCTRL capture sequence. A response code is not independently cleared by software.

codes.title: Native data-plane rejection reasons

meanings.FaultUnmapped: Address does not select a decoded data target.
meanings.FaultInactivePad: QPI/OPI access targets the inactive memory-pad mode.
meanings.FaultAccess: Initiator access policy rejects the request.
meanings.FaultProtocol: Request violates the admitted AXI transaction subset.

codes.observation: Fabric Monitor FAULT reason, with master/target/direction/address. These native AXI reasons are not the RIB/SYSCTRL reason enumeration.
codes.handling: Capture the monitor record and clear under its CONTROL contract. A clear neither widens access nor reactivates an isolated target.

codes.title: Native data-plane target timeout

meanings.FaultTimeout: Target guard reports a timed-out transaction and isolation state.

codes.observation: Same Fabric Monitor native reason namespace as the rejection table. Inspect target guard/isolation status.
codes.handling: Stop new work and follow the target recovery/reset contract before reuse. Clearing the monitor record alone does not reconnect the target.

codes.title: PLL transaction result

meanings.0: No transaction error; force-safe may also report zero.
meanings.2: Quiesce, lock-low observation or lock qualification timed out.

codes.observation: SYSCTRL PLL_STATUS error reason; also inspect valid, safe-clock and current lock bits.
codes.handling: Retain the error with clock state. Clear the appropriate sticky indication only after diagnosis; zero does not alone prove PLL operation.

codes.title: Central DMA channel error code

meanings.DMA_ERROR_AXI_READ: AXI read returned a non-OKAY response.
meanings.DMA_ERROR_AXI_WRITE: AXI write returned a non-OKAY response.
meanings.DMA_ERROR_STREAM: Stream transfer framing or acceptance error.

codes.observation: CH_ERROR_STATUS low nibble; response, direction and stream-last flags occupy separate fields. Capture CH_ERROR_ADDR and completed byte count.
codes.handling: Use channel event/IRQ acknowledgement and the documented submit/recovery sequence; do not write a read-only error code as an acknowledgement.

codes.title: SDIO private DMA ABI masks
codes.observation: Published SDK mask values, not ordinal numbers. The shared SDIO/SPI-SD engine currently emits one cause mask at a time; it uses 0x02 for its invalid-start check. The SDK 0x01 declaration is not emitted by the reviewed engine.
codes.handling: Preserve DMA and controller errors before local IRQ/error W1C; reinitialize the transfer only after the engine has stopped.

codes.title: USB2 DMA engine error codes
codes.observation: ERROR_CODE low byte captures a DMA engine code for DMA faults. Scheduler packet faults instead encode 0x80 OR the transfer-result nibble; capture the associated ERROR_STATUS and ERROR_INFO.
codes.handling: Record ERROR_DESC_ADDR and ERROR_BUFFER_ADDR before local W1C. A zero-initialized code is not a successful completion without the corresponding valid/done state.

codes.title: USB2 descriptor validation codes
codes.observation: Descriptor validation result; distinguish it from the USB2 packet result and descriptor completion bits.
codes.handling: Fix ownership, geometry or reserved fields after software owns the descriptor; preserve ERROR_CODE/INFO and descriptor/buffer addresses.

codes.title: USB2 transfer result codes

meanings.Usb2ResultNak: NAK response; handle according to transfer/scheduling policy.

codes.observation: Internal transfer result consumed by scheduling/writeback. Decode the corresponding public descriptor status, endpoint/channel status and error record.
codes.handling: These values are not a universal encoding of ERROR_CODE. Complete descriptor ownership and local acknowledgement before resubmission.

codes.title: JPEG job error codes
codes.observation: ERROR_STATUS code and stage, ERROR_ADDRESS/DETAIL and descriptor result. A declared code does not prove the system payload path is usable.
codes.handling: Copy the first error before ERROR_STATUS/IRQ_STATE W1C and follow ring/direct-job recovery. The reviewed native master-credit limitation still applies.

codes.title: APU declared error codes
codes.observation: ERROR_STATUS code, stage, AXI response and descriptor index; ERROR_ADDRESS/DETAIL provide context.
codes.handling: Preserve the first error, then apply the documented ERROR_STATUS/IRQ_STATE acknowledgement. Declared codec/KWS codes do not establish implemented production features.

codes.title: SDK rs_status_t return values

meanings.RS_OK: Operation completed under that API contract.

codes.observation: Signed API return value. Exact triggering conditions depend on the called function; the enum definition does not make every code reachable from every API.
codes.handling: Check the return before using output values. No hardware W1C applies to a C return value; preserve the relevant peripheral status if diagnosis requires it.

status_registers.title: Clock, memory-pad and HP lifecycle observations
status_registers.observation: Clock command response 0 means accepted and 1 means rejected; the controller validates selectors, idle state, nonzero timeout and memory-pad lock. Read requested and actual HP state together.
status_registers.handling: PLL/clock fault clear and memory-pad fault clear are distinct commands. HP forced-fault records cache-clean, drain or flush timeout and clears on reset/new release under its lifecycle contract.

bindings.text: 21'd0, pll_ctrl.capable_i, s_pll_lock_q, s_pll_safe_clk_q, s_pll_err_reason_q, s_pll_err_q, s_pll_busy_q, s_pll_active_valid_q, s_pll_active_sel_q
26'd0, sysctrl.hp_actual_released_i, sysctrl.hp_forced_fault_i, sysctrl.hp_draining_i, sysctrl.hp_present_i && !s_hp_release_q, s_hp_release_q, sysctrl.hp_present_i

main.PLL_STATUS.name: CAPABLE

clock.CLK_STATUS.name: RESPONSE_REJECTED
clock.CLK_STATUS.description: Last AON clock command response was nonzero.

clock.MEM_PAD_FAULT.name: PAD_CONFIG_FAULT
clock.MEM_PAD_FAULT.description: Rejected memory-pad configuration observed; use its dedicated clear command.

main.HP_STATUS.name: PRESENT
main.HP_STATUS.description: HP is present in this implementation.

main.HP_STATUS.name: REQUESTED_HOLD
main.HP_STATUS.description: HP present and release request is clear; this is not an independent observation of actual reset.

main.HP_STATUS.name: FORCED_FAULT
main.HP_STATUS.description: A cache, drain or flush timeout forced lifecycle progress.

status_registers.title: Resource ownership fault
status_registers.observation: FAULT is one sticky bit, not an encoded reason. A rejected OWNER write sets it; inspect owner lock, quiesce, block acknowledgement and idle state to determine the cause.
status_registers.handling: Capture STATUS before full-word W1C of FAULT bit 0. Clearing does not change owner or unlock the resource.

status_registers.title: Central DMA completion and error observations
status_registers.observation: Use CH_ERROR_ADDR, bytes completed and descriptor status with these fields. ERROR_STATUS and channel events have distinct purposes.
status_registers.handling: Acknowledge local W1C event/IRQ fields according to the DMA contract; preserve read-only error detail before a new channel command changes it.

ch.ERROR_STATUS.name: CODE
ch.ERROR_STATUS.description: Central DMA error enumeration in the code table.

ch.ERROR_STATUS.name: READ
ch.ERROR_STATUS.description: One identifies the read side of the reported error.

status_registers.title: SPI-SD private DMA status
status_registers.observation: SPI-SD has its own DMA register semantics. Capture DMA_ERROR_ADDR, command/data completion and actual transfer count.
status_registers.handling: Copy the error snapshot before ERROR_STATUS and IRQ_STATUS W1C. Do not substitute the central DMA nibble enumeration.

status_registers.title: SDIO0/1 private DMA status
status_registers.observation: Decode against the selected SDIO instance. The mask table above applies to DMA_ERROR; controller ERROR_STATUS remains a separate cause set.
status_registers.handling: Capture DMA_ERROR_ADDR and controller errors, stop/abort as required, then acknowledge local interrupt/error state.

status_registers.title: USB2 first error record
status_registers.observation: Capture ERROR_DESC_ADDR and ERROR_BUFFER_ADDR plus endpoint/channel state and descriptor completion. Internal result and descriptor-validation enums are separate namespaces.
status_registers.handling: Follow USB2 ERROR_STATUS/IRQ_STATUS W1C and descriptor ownership rules. A packet retry is a scheduler/transfer-policy decision.

main.ERROR_STATUS.name: SCHEDULER_FAULT
main.ERROR_STATUS.description: Scheduler/DMA first-fault event, latched and W1C in the register block.

main.ERROR_CODE.name: CODE
main.ERROR_CODE.description: DMA engine error code, or 0x80 OR packet-result nibble for scheduler packet faults.

main.ERROR_INFO.name: INDEX
main.ERROR_INFO.description: Affected device endpoint or host channel.

status_registers.title: JPEG first error record
status_registers.observation: Capture ERROR_ADDRESS, ring position and descriptor status with the error code/stage.
status_registers.handling: Acknowledge only after recording the first failure. The documented zero-credit system limitation remains in force.

status_registers.title: APU first error record
status_registers.observation: Capture ERROR_ADDRESS, ring position and stream state. The enum covers the declared ABI; production availability is qualified in the APU/system chapters.
status_registers.handling: Preserve error details before W1C; recover descriptor/stream ownership under the APU contract.

status_registers.title: EXT-H DMA and slot fault
status_registers.observation: FAULT is sticky; DMA_STATUS contains busy, a completion pulse and fault. Capture FAULT_ADDRESS. EXT-L reads zero in its DMA status view.
status_registers.handling: The slot COMMAND clear operation controls the sticky fault; DMA done is a pulse, not a W1C completion register. Preserve software completion state before it disappears.

main.DmaStatus.name: DONE_PULSE
main.DmaStatus.description: EXT-H one-cycle DMA completion observation; software must account for the interrupt/handler timing.

main.DmaStatus.name: FAULT
main.DmaStatus.description: EXT-H sticky slot/DMA fault. EXT-L returns zero for this whole register.

meanings.1: UART initialization failed; terminal failure is written directly without requiring a printable console.
meanings.3: SDRAM did not reach the required ready/error-free state within the firmware wait.
meanings.4: Bundle header or bounds/format validation failed.
meanings.5: DMA and software copy/CRC fallback failed for bundle entry index 0.
meanings.6: DMA and software copy/CRC fallback failed for bundle entry index 1.
meanings.7: DMA and software copy/CRC fallback failed for bundle entry index 2.
meanings.8: DMA and software copy/CRC fallback failed for bundle entry index 3.
meanings.9: Mailbox clear, HP release request or released-state check failed.
meanings.10: Nonzero-sequence mailbox message did not carry the expected Linux-ready event/argument.

applications.title: Bringup application
applications.selection: Default APP=bringup in the publication reference profile.
applications.prerequisites: Complete generic LP startup and memory initialization; provide the reviewed peripheral configuration and LP ownership. The routine changes interrupt-test and Crypto state.

stages.title: Initialize UART0
stages.coverage: Initialize the LP diagnostic console.
stages.boundary: Failure returns from main without writing TEST_STATUS; generic CRT then loops.

stages.title: SDIO0 controller discovery / IRQ
stages.coverage: Probe controller, check PIO/CRC capability and presence; inject/read/clear CMD_DONE.
stages.boundary: Does not initialize an SD card or transfer card data.

stages.title: USB2 controller discovery / IRQ
stages.coverage: Probe the controller, require idle and observe an injected fatal-status IRQ.
stages.boundary: Does not enumerate a device or exercise a ULPI packet transfer.

stages.title: Crypto known-answer self-test
stages.coverage: AES-128 ECB encryption and SHA-256 known answers, followed by zeroization.
stages.boundary: Does not cover every AES mode, SHA variant, RSA or streaming/DMA combination.

stages.title: Completed selected checks
stages.coverage: All preceding terminal checks returned success.
stages.boundary: ARCHINFO diagnostic text has no separately propagated terminal result in this application.

applications.title: CI smoke application
applications.selection: Selected by the regression runner with APP=ci_smoke on the selected supported profile; not the default reference application.
applications.prerequisites: Reserve the scratch SRAM/SDRAM regions and GPIO31, stop competing users and use the matching PRODUCT map. Source-present checks are not an instruction to run this destructive scratch test on a live workload.

stages.title: Initialize UART0
stages.coverage: Initialize the console.
stages.boundary: Failure can precede usable UART output.

stages.title: UART v3 loopback
stages.coverage: Check version/capability; transmit and receive one internal-loopback byte; restore console configuration.
stages.boundary: No board TX/RX or hardware-flow-control qualification.

stages.title: ARCHINFO and RTC probe
stages.coverage: Validate build identity, expected unsupported device-ID read and RTC probe.
stages.boundary: No unique silicon identity or RTC accuracy qualification.

stages.title: APU discovery
stages.coverage: Compare APU discovery capabilities and ABI digest.
stages.boundary: No production codec job is submitted.

stages.title: Start Fabric Monitor
stages.coverage: Clear and enable monitoring before memory traffic.
stages.boundary: Code 13 also identifies the later monitor-observation stage.

stages.title: SRAM discovery and memory accesses
stages.coverage: Check presence/size/banks; exercise byte/halfword/word lanes and boundary storage when present.
stages.boundary: Writes scratch memory; not an exhaustive memory or ECC test. Code 12 is also used by USB2.

stages.title: Inspect Fabric Monitor
stages.coverage: Snapshot LP/target traffic and require nonzero reads/writes without recorded fault or flush.
stages.boundary: No throughput, latency or long-run fault-coverage claim.

stages.title: PRODUCT extension control
stages.coverage: Probe EXT-L/H, reject MPW selection and EXT-L ACL configuration; exercise EXT-H ACL/lifecycle.
stages.boundary: Does not execute an EXT-H DMA workload.

stages.title: RNG diagnostic source
stages.coverage: Read changing diagnostic words, check source state and expected entropy rejection.
stages.boundary: Does not qualify entropy or cryptographic randomness.

stages.title: Management CLINT access
stages.coverage: Observe time progress; write/read compare and software-pending state; restore compare.
stages.boundary: Polling register behavior does not demonstrate trap-handler delivery.

stages.title: Timer0 one-shot
stages.coverage: Configure/start down-counting one-shot; poll stopped state and timeout/compare flags.
stages.boundary: No CPU ISR, waveform or pad timing measurement.

stages.title: Timer1 periodic
stages.coverage: Configure up-counting periodic timer; poll timeout/compare flags and stop.
stages.boundary: No guaranteed interrupt latency or accuracy result.

stages.title: GPIO31 output controls
stages.coverage: Check capabilities; configure, write, toggle and clear output 31.
stages.boundary: Changes a GPIO output; no independent external voltage/readback measurement.

stages.title: SDRAM scratch access
stages.coverage: Wait for ready; byte/halfword/word write and readback in the last 16 mapped bytes.
stages.boundary: Destructive scratch test; not an exhaustive device/timing test.

stages.title: Crypto known-answer self-test
stages.coverage: Run the same AES/SHA/zeroization routine as bringup.
stages.boundary: Does not extend that routine to other algorithms or DMA paths.

stages.title: USB2 controller self-test
stages.coverage: Run the same discovery/idle/IRQ test as bringup.
stages.boundary: Code 12 also identifies SRAM failures; retain stage logs.

stages.title: Completed selected checks
stages.coverage: All preceding selected checks passed.
stages.boundary: The printed summary covers this sequence, not every SoC peripheral or operating mode.

api_semantics.name: rs_wait_mask
api_semantics.budget: At most timeout loop iterations/read attempts after input checks.
api_semantics.zero: With valid input, return RS_ETIMEOUT without reading the register.
api_semantics.success: A register sample satisfied the predicate: the masked register equals expected.
api_semantics.failure: The helper performs no command, abort or reset. Its register reads can still have the target register's side effects.
api_semantics.next: Check input validity and the owning IP state before retrying. A polling budget is not a wall-clock deadline.

api_semantics.name: rs_wait_value
api_semantics.budget: At most timeout loop iterations/read attempts after input checks.
api_semantics.zero: With valid input, return RS_ETIMEOUT without reading the register.
api_semantics.success: A register sample satisfied the predicate: the register equals expected.
api_semantics.failure: The helper performs no command, abort or reset. Its register reads can still have the target register's side effects.
api_semantics.next: Check input validity and the owning IP state before retrying. A polling budget is not a wall-clock deadline.

api_semantics.name: rs_wait_not_value
api_semantics.budget: At most timeout loop iterations/read attempts after input checks.
api_semantics.zero: With valid input, return RS_ETIMEOUT without reading the register.
api_semantics.success: A register sample satisfied the predicate: the register differs from value.
api_semantics.failure: The helper performs no command, abort or reset. Its register reads can still have the target register's side effects.
api_semantics.next: Check input validity and the owning IP state before retrying. A polling budget is not a wall-clock deadline.

api_semantics.name: rs_uart_write
api_semantics.budget: One budget is shared across the call and consumed only while TX_FULL is observed.
api_semantics.zero: Can write when FIFO space is immediately available; otherwise return RS_ETIMEOUT at the first required wait. Zero length succeeds.
api_semantics.success: All requested bytes were written to TXDATA. The final serial bit need not have left the pin.
api_semantics.failure: A prefix may already be queued or transmitted. No transferred-length result, automatic abort or rollback is returned.
api_semantics.next: Use protocol-level framing and status before deciding what can be retried; blind replay can duplicate bytes.

api_semantics.name: rs_uart_read
api_semantics.budget: One budget is shared across the call and consumed only while RX_EMPTY is observed.
api_semantics.zero: Can consume immediately available bytes; otherwise return RS_ETIMEOUT at the first required wait. Zero length succeeds.
api_semantics.success: The requested number of RX entries was consumed and written into the caller buffer, including per-entry error bits.
api_semantics.failure: Earlier entries may already have been popped and copied. The API does not return the completed prefix length.
api_semantics.next: Validate entry error fields on success; use a protocol-aware receive/recovery policy after partial failure.

api_semantics.name: rs_dma_start
api_semantics.budget: No timeout argument; no completion polling.
api_semantics.success: For a valid channel, software cleared event flags and wrote START. It did not independently confirm command admission or completion.
api_semantics.failure: An invalid channel is rejected locally; hardware may later report a command or transfer error.
api_semantics.next: Observe channel status and completion/error records before consuming output or reusing buffers.

api_semantics.name: rs_dma_abort
api_semantics.budget: No timeout argument; no drain polling.
api_semantics.success: For a valid channel, the ABORT command was written. Accepted transactions may still be draining.
api_semantics.failure: The return does not confirm that BUSY is clear or that the buffer is reusable.
api_semantics.next: Use rs_dma_abort_wait or an equivalent status/drain observation, then preserve completion and error details.

api_semantics.name: rs_dma_abort_wait
api_semantics.budget: Send ABORT, then perform up to timeout status polls.
api_semantics.zero: Still sends ABORT for a valid channel, then returns RS_ETIMEOUT without a status poll.
api_semantics.success: A status read succeeded and BUSY was clear; it does not require a particular abort/error flag combination.
api_semantics.failure: RS_ETIMEOUT does not establish that draining finished. The command has already been issued.
api_semantics.next: Keep buffers owned until a later idle/drain confirmation; inspect the final reason flags separately.

api_semantics.name: rs_dma_wait
api_semantics.budget: Up to timeout status polls; error/aborted is tested before DONE.
api_semantics.zero: For a valid channel, return RS_ETIMEOUT without reading status.
api_semantics.success: A status sample showed DONE without the error or aborted flags.
api_semantics.failure: Returns RS_EIO for an observed error/abort; exhaustion returns RS_ETIMEOUT without issuing ABORT.
api_semantics.next: Retain ownership and inspect progress; if stopping is required, request abort and confirm drain before reusing storage.

api_semantics.name: rs_timer_delay_ms
api_semantics.budget: milliseconds selects the hardware period; timeout independently bounds status-loop iterations.
api_semantics.zero: Zero milliseconds succeeds for a valid timer. With a positive delay, zero timeout still configures/starts the timer, then attempts stop and returns RS_ETIMEOUT.
api_semantics.success: Zero duration was requested, or a status sample showed the configured one-shot no longer active.
api_semantics.failure: On loop exhaustion it calls rs_timer_stop, ignores that return and reports RS_ETIMEOUT. Earlier configuration/start errors do not provide a general rollback guarantee.
api_semantics.next: This helper reconfigures the selected timer. Reserve it, and confirm state explicitly if recovery depends on successful stopping.

header_fields.magic: Format marker written as a little-endian 32-bit word.
header_fields.version: Bundle format version; distinct from the datasheet revision.
header_fields.header_size: Bytes in the fixed header plus all entry descriptors.
header_fields.total_size: Bundle-relative byte extent from BUNDLE_OFFSET through the aligned image end; includes gaps and padding.
header_fields.header_crc32: CRC of the complete header/entry area with this field zeroed.
header_fields.flags: Generator writes REQUIRED; loader requires its bit to be set.
header_fields.reserved: Generator writes zero; loader has no independent zero-value check for this field.

entry_fields.type: Fixed artifact type in the expected OpenSBI, DTB, Linux, initramfs order.
entry_fields.flash_offset: Absolute offset from the start of the flash image, not from the bundle header.
entry_fields.load_address: Fixed destination address in the selected SDRAM map.
entry_fields.size: Nonzero payload byte count; excludes alignment padding.
entry_fields.crc32: CRC of exactly size payload bytes.
entry_fields.flags: Generator writes REQUIRED; loader requires its bit to be set.

rules.producer: Little-endian 32-bit words, eight fixed-header words and six words per entry.
rules.loader: Copies the header into the RV32 C structure and interprets its words; no alternative byte-order negotiation.
rules.consequence: Use the declared byte format; do not serialize an arbitrary host structure with native packing.

rules.producer: Four artifacts in fixed order, with the prescribed load address and maximum size for each.
rules.loader: Checks exact type/order/load address and the per-artifact maximum, plus nonzero size and mapped ranges.
rules.consequence: This is not a generic relocatable image table.

rules.producer: Computes the complete header CRC with its CRC word zero; computes each payload CRC before padding.
rules.loader: Zeroes the header CRC word in its local copy before comparison; payload checks follow the existing DMA/copy path.
rules.consequence: Padding bytes are not payload CRC input; CRC detects corruption, not origin or rollback.

rules.producer: Aligns each payload start and the final cursor to PAYLOAD_ALIGNMENT.
rules.loader: Checks flash_offset and load_address modulo four, not the generator's larger boundary.
rules.consequence: Generated layout and accepted alignment are different conditions.

rules.loader: Requires the REQUIRED bit in header and entries. Does not independently reject extra flag bits or nonzero reserved.
rules.consequence: Preserve canonical generator values; do not claim strict reserved-bit rejection.

rules.producer: Places payloads sequentially without overlap, filling unused image bytes with 0xFF.
rules.loader: Bounds each entry within the bundle/SDRAM ranges; does not independently enforce sequential disjoint extents or padding values.
rules.consequence: Do not confuse deterministic output layout with stronger validation that is absent from the loader.

rules.producer: Rejects LP firmware beyond the bundle start, empty/oversized payloads and an aligned image beyond FLASH_SIZE.
rules.loader: Checks header size/count, bundle total limits and each entry's source/destination bounds.
rules.consequence: Per-artifact maximum allocations do not mean all maximum-sized artifacts fit simultaneously in flash.
